song.title: You Can't Always Get What You Want

guitar.guitaristsText: Keith Richards / Ronnie Wood / Mick Taylor
guitar.modelsText: Fender Telecaster ('Micawber', 5-string open-G) / Gibson Les Paul / ES series
guitar.evidence: Keith Richards' 5-string open-G-tuned Telecaster 'Micawber' is one of the most famous specific guitars in rock history; this justifies high rather than medium confidence.
guitar.notes: Upgraded confidence from medium to high due to Richards' very specifically documented guitar/tuning setup.

tone.target: warm 60s strummed clean with slight breakup
tone.profile: warm 60s strummed clean with slight breakup
tone.summary: A warm, strummed 60s tone achieved using a classic British amp model (UK 45) paired with minimal compression and light delay for an acoustic-electric feel.
corrections: shift from electric crunch to strummed acoustic feel

rig.name: The Rolling Stones - You Can't Always Get What You Want - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Smooth out dynamics and add sustain for a strummed acoustic feel.
blocks.gap: The Comp module is ideal for the 'acoustic strum feel' requirement, though no specific settings are provided.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone clean and avoid heavy distortion or modern overdrive.
blocks.gap: The 'None' setting is used to ensure no unwanted drive coloration interferes with the vintage clean sound.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British 'small tube amp' sound with natural, light breakup.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is a good proxy for vintage small tube amps, fitting the 60s vibe and required light breakup.

blocks.purpose: Achieve the required 'dry close-mic texture' and vintage British sound.
blocks.gap: The UK Vintage 4x12 is chosen for its classic British voicing, matching the era and tone requirement.

blocks.purpose: Slightly scoop the mids and tame excessive high frequencies for a warmer, vintage mono vibe.
blocks.gap: Used to fine-tune the frequency response towards a warm 60s sound profile.

blocks.purpose: No wah needed; keep the tone natural and focused on strumming.
blocks.gap: The 'None' setting ensures no unwanted filtering or coloration.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone dry and focused on strumming; Chorus is unnecessary.
blocks.gap: The 'None' approach (by deactivating or using a minimal setting) is best for this clean, vintage sound. Using Chorus would add unwanted movement.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle depth and space without distracting from the strumming rhythm.
blocks.gap: A light delay adds 'air' and helps fill out the sound, mimicking vintage recording techniques.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle sense of space and warmth without sounding overly wet or modern.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is ideal for achieving the 'dry close-mic texture' while adding necessary vintage ambience.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the IR to better capture a vintage, dry close-mic sound suitable for 60s strumming.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage, dry close-mic texture required for 60s strumming.
